question: What is the product of all positive odd integers less than \(10{,}000?\)
solution:
A factorial includes all the consecutive positive integers up to its argument: \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots n\). This lets us obtain the desired odd product by removing the even factors from \(10000!\).

Let \(P=1\cdot3\cdot5\cdots9999\). Every factor in \(10000!\) is either one of these odd numbers or an even number, so
\[
10000!=P(2\cdot4\cdot6\cdots10000).
\]
There are \(5000\) even factors, each contributing a factor of \(2\). Thus
\[
2\cdot4\cdots10000
=2^{5000}(1\cdot2\cdots5000)
=2^{5000}\cdot5000!.
\]
Dividing by this positive product gives
\[
P=\boxed{\frac{10000!}{2^{5000}\cdot5000!}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
